title: Resources
key_points: Resources are data containers in Godot that do not perform actions on their own.
Examples of resources include Texture, Script, Mesh, Animation, AudioStream, Font, and Translation.
When the engine loads a resource from disk, it only loads it once. If a copy is already in memory, trying to load the resource again returns the same copy every time.
limitations: The documentation provides general information but does not cover all possible scenarios or edge cases for resources in Godot.
The scope and relevance of the content may vary depending on the specific needs and context of a user learning about resources.
The provided examples are simplified and may not fully represent real-world usage.
asserts: Resources in Godot provide a way to store and manage data separate from nodes, allowing for efficient reuse and sharing of data across different parts of a project.
scope: The context of the content is focused on explaining the concept and use of resources within the Godot game engine, specifically how they differ from and interact with nodes.
